comparator.name: Geschiedenis
comparator.academicYear: Prospective coherent sequence: year 1 (2027–28), year 2 (2028–29), year 3 (2029–30), checked 2026-09-25
comparator.sourceNotes: The prospective pages describe a coherent chronological student path: 60 EC in each year. Year one counts seven credited courses (5+10+10+10+10+10+5); the zero-credit mentorship is excluded. Year two includes 30 EC in compulsory courses, including one 10-EC thematic research seminar and 5-EC environmental history, plus two permitted 15-EC humanities minors. Year three uses the domestic option: 10-EC thematic seminar, two 5-EC career/historical reflection courses, 10-EC bachelor essay and 30-EC genuinely free space. The year-two minors and year-three free space do not receive invented disciplinary subjects. Seminar examples change by year. All three annual pages describe indicative future offerings, subject to change.
components: Methods and Techniques of the Historian

One permitted humanities minor; the example does not assign invented subjects.
A second permitted 15-EC humanities minor; exact field remains elective.
One year-three thematic research seminar; offered topics can change.
Genuine elective space for courses, internship, exchange or educational minor; no content invented.

core: Historical inquiry across ancient, medieval, early modern and contemporary periods
Critical interpretation of sources, historiography and independent research writing
Political, social, cultural, gender and religious change in history
Historical connections and globalisation as lenses for present-day questions
adjacent: Material culture, archaeology, art and heritage as evidence about the past
Modern visual and media culture and contested historical memory
questions: How do accounts of empires, war, identity and gender change with the evidence and the historian’s perspective?
How can historical research place current social and political developments in context?

alternatives.label: History, empire and political change
alternatives.concept: A historical and interdisciplinary course of study centred on modern history, empires, warfare, gender, Indigenous histories and historical research, interpreted alongside archaeology, art and media evidence and the politics of international and European change. UCR has limited dedicated period surveys and no required archive-based bachelor thesis in History.
alternatives.labelReason: The six actual History courses anchor a sustained historical sequence; archaeology, art, media and political studies explicitly specify its material evidence and political emphasis.
progression: Modern History and introductory material culture and political courses precede upper-level history, heritage and research work where semester offerings allow; all formal prerequisites and course availability pass.

alternatives.label: Cultural histories and heritage
alternatives.concept: A distinct historically oriented UCR programme focused on material culture, world archaeology, art and museum practice, media history, gender and race, literary texts, and historical interpretation. It retains all six UCR History courses and adds multiple upper-level methods and heritage courses.
alternatives.labelReason: The six History courses combine with a sustained archaeology, art heritage and historical media sequence including advanced museum and historiography work.
progression: Introductory world archaeology, art history, historical survey and media study precede museum, heritage, advanced history and critical literary interpretation where available; all formal prerequisites and published semesters pass.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the first programme, five political and international-relations courses give way to African art and heritage, film and documentary history, literary interpretation and further museum and heritage study. This changes the source base, research questions and upper-level disciplinary progression, while preserving the shared History core.

candidates.label: Secondary-school history teaching
candidates.reason: Radboud offers a history educational minor with school practice and a teaching qualification in combination with its bachelor. The UCR catalogue does not provide pedagogical training, school placements or a certified history teacher route.

candidates.label: Historian’s independent archive and source research
candidates.reason: Historical research is already represented by History Research Seminar and additional critical interpretation of visual and textual evidence in the first programme. It cannot be presented as an equivalent to the formally required archive laboratory and History bachelor essay.

routeSelection.basis: The published domestic third-year option leaves 30 EC of broadly selectable open space, whereas the study-abroad option explicitly requires it to be used for an exchange. No registry interest requires a period abroad.

selection.assessment: Two credible 24-course responses are distinct in focus: political and global history versus cultural and material heritage. A formal teaching track is unavailable at UCR; a separate archive-specialist track would duplicate the existing History Research Seminar without the depth of the Radboud archive and thesis requirements.

notes.text: UCR offers six History courses and significant archaeology, art, media and political study. Radboud History has a more extensive chronological period sequence, an archive-focused research laboratory, two thematic historical seminars and a required independent History bachelor essay; UCR’s related projects are not formal equivalents to those requirements.
